notes:
Quick summary: inbound SMB (self-serve) that signed up via free tier and started integrating chat for their support widget. Primary complaint: perceived slowness from web/mobile clients, especially for EU customers. They are cost sensitive and want clear guidance they can implement without a Dedicated commitment.

Timeline / activity (recent):
- 2026-02-24: Signup + initial API key used in staging (frontend widget).
- 2026-03-01: First support email reporting slow responses from end users in Berlin (FF call id ff_20260301_9238).
- 2026-03-02: AE (Ava) intro call; collected logs and a short HAR from customer. Noted many requests going to us-east by default.
- 2026-03-03: SE (Diego) quick perf probe: synthetic curl runs from Frankfurt -> us-east-1 returned median TTFB ~420ms, p95 ~950ms; calls routed to us-east rather than eu-west-1.
- 2026-03-04: Sent debug checklist + asked for sample request payloads and average prompt lengths. Customer replied with sample prompts (~90-220 tokens user + 1 system ~100 tokens).

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "Users complain the chat feels laggy on mobile  — sometimes it times out."
- "We assumed hosted would be fast; surprised hits go to US region even for EU customers."

Observed pain points and root causes (SE notes):
- Region mismatch: SDK default / browser origin leading to requests terminating in us-east for EU users.
- Long system prompts + chat history: large context increases model compute time.
- No client-side streaming: waiting for full response increases perceived latency.
- Mobile clients have low request timeouts; using 6s read timeout causes premature timeouts when p95 is near 1s plus network jitter.

Perf tuning recommendations given (technical):
- Region choice: configure requests to nearest Redwood hosted region (recommend eu-west-1 for EU customers). Show how to set region in the SDK and REST endpoint examples (shared in Drive).
- Timeouts: client defaults we recommend: connect timeout 1s, read/response timeout 12s for chat on mobile; desktop web can use 20s. Encourage exponential backoff + safe retry for idempotent operations.
- Prompt guidance: reduce system prompt length; prefer a short system + reference documents via embedding lookup instead of sending full doc text. Trim chat history to last N relevant turns (N=3 by default). Aim for median request < 350 tokens.
- Streaming: enable streaming for chat so the UI displays token-by-token and perceived latency drops. Show example to switch on streaming in SDK snippets.
- Model variant: suggest testing a faster flavor of same family (e.g., ridge-1-mini) for user-facing low-latency endpoints; reserve larger models for async tasks (summaries, batch jobs).
- Instrumentation: add simple timing headers (X-Req-Start) and capture server-side request_id to correlate with Redwood logs; attach examples of what to look for in Console latency dashboard.
- Caching: enable short-term prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (e.g., standard greetings, menu prompts).

Action items / next steps agreed:
- I (Ava) to send concise perf tuning checklist + sample SDK snippets by 2026-03-06 (done).
- SE Diego to share quick curl commands and region endpoint examples; customer to run from their EU test runner and paste traces.
- Customer to try streaming and shorten system prompt, report p95 after changes (internal target: p95 < 700ms for EU).
- Schedule 15-20m technical follow-up after they run tests (target week of 2026-03-08).

Open questions / blockers:
- They want clarity on any cost delta when switching regions (we sent the hosted pricing doc).
- Mobile SDK guidance for reconnects: customer requests snippet for incremental streaming + reconnection strategy.

Notes about engagement tone: Quick-moving SMB — pragmatic, wants actionable steps they can implement this week. Good PLG candidate to convert with low-touch docs + measurable perf gains.

References & artifacts: Fireflies ff_20260301_9238 (call transcript), Drive: /drive/wildberry/wildberry-hosted-api-perf-notes.pdf, Jira RB-3421 (customer reported timeouts).
